package: plug-in development board, 2 × 19 header pins at 2.54 mm (J2, J3), micro-USB

datasheet.title: ESP32 esp-dev-kits Documentation, Release master (2025-11-24), chapter 1.1 ESP32-DevKitC V4

1.name: 3V3
1.hint: output of the board's AMS1117-3.3 (U2 of the DevKitC V4 schematic) that feeds the module; the header's 3V3 pin – as a supply input it is one of the three mutually exclusive ways to power the board (ESP32 esp-dev-kits Documentation, Release master (Espressif, 2025-11-24), 1.1 ESP32-DevKitC V4, 1.1.4)

2.name: EN
2.hint: CHIP_PU of the module, reset when low (VIL_nRST ≤ 0.6 V, release at ≥ 0.75 × VDD, ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 table 15); on the board 10 kΩ to 3V3 (R11) and 100 nF (C9), the EN button with 100 nF (C14) – DevKitC V4 schematic; a 3.3 V pin: VIH up to VDD + 0.3 V

3.name: VP
3.hint: GPIO36: input only – no output driver, no internal pull-up or pull-down (ESP32 Series Datasheet v5.3, table 6-1 note 2)

4.name: VN
4.hint: GPIO39: input only – no output driver, no internal pull-up or pull-down (ESP32 Series Datasheet v5.3, table 6-1 note 2)

5.name: IO34
5.hint: GPIO34: input only – no output driver, no internal pull-up or pull-down (ESP32 Series Datasheet v5.3, table 6-1 note 2)

6.name: IO35
6.hint: GPIO35: input only – no output driver, no internal pull-up or pull-down (ESP32 Series Datasheet v5.3, table 6-1 note 2)

9.name: IO25
9.hint: ADC2: shared with Wi-Fi (ESP-IDF v6.1 ADC oneshot driver, Hardware Limitations) – an analog read competes with the Wi-Fi driver

10.name: IO26
10.hint: ADC2: shared with Wi-Fi (ESP-IDF v6.1 ADC oneshot driver, Hardware Limitations) – an analog read competes with the Wi-Fi driver

11.name: IO27
11.hint: ADC2: shared with Wi-Fi (ESP-IDF v6.1 ADC oneshot driver, Hardware Limitations) – an analog read competes with the Wi-Fi driver

12.name: IO14
12.hint: ADC2: shared with Wi-Fi (ESP-IDF v6.1 ADC oneshot driver, Hardware Limitations) – an analog read competes with the Wi-Fi driver

13.name: IO12
13.hint: strapping pin MTDI: high at reset sets VDD_SDIO to 1.8 V; datasheet figure 9: 'IO12 should be kept low when the module is powered on' (datasheet 4.2, table 4); ADC2: shared with Wi-Fi (ESP-IDF v6.1 ADC oneshot driver, Hardware Limitations) – an analog read competes with the Wi-Fi driver

15.name: IO13
15.hint: ADC2: shared with Wi-Fi (ESP-IDF v6.1 ADC oneshot driver, Hardware Limitations) – an analog read competes with the Wi-Fi driver

16.name: D2
16.hint: GPIO9: the flash pins, not led out of the ESP32-WROVER-E (ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 table 3, pins 17–22, note 2) – the header pin carries nothing here

17.name: D3
17.hint: GPIO10: the flash pins, not led out of the ESP32-WROVER-E (ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 table 3, pins 17–22, note 2) – the header pin carries nothing here

18.name: CMD
18.hint: GPIO11: the flash pins, not led out of the ESP32-WROVER-E (ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 table 3, pins 17–22, note 2) – the header pin carries nothing here

19.name: 5V
19.hint: EXT_5V of the DevKitC V4 schematic: the input of the board's AMS1117-3.3, fed from the micro-USB VBUS through the board's Schottky diode (BAT760) – power the board through one and only one of micro-USB, 5V or 3V3 (ESP32 esp-dev-kits Documentation, Release master (Espressif, 2025-11-24), 1.1 ESP32-DevKitC V4, 1.1.4, warning)

23.name: TX
23.hint: U0TXD: UART0 downloads firmware and prints the log (datasheet 9 Peripheral Schematics)

24.name: RX
24.hint: U0RXD: UART0 downloads firmware and prints the log (datasheet 9 Peripheral Schematics)

29.name: IO5
29.hint: strapping pin GPIO5: with MTDO it sets the SDIO slave timing; weak pull-up at reset (datasheet table 4, 8)

30.name: IO17
30.hint: GPIO17: NC on the ESP32-WROVER-E, the module's PSRAM uses it (ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 table 3, pins 27–28; ESP32 esp-dev-kits Documentation, Release master (Espressif, 2025-11-24), 1.1 ESP32-DevKitC V4, J3 note 3) – the header pin carries nothing here

31.name: IO16
31.hint: GPIO16: NC on the ESP32-WROVER-E, the module's PSRAM uses it (ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 table 3, pins 27–28; ESP32 esp-dev-kits Documentation, Release master (Espressif, 2025-11-24), 1.1 ESP32-DevKitC V4, J3 note 3) – the header pin carries nothing here

32.name: IO4
32.hint: ADC2: shared with Wi-Fi (ESP-IDF v6.1 ADC oneshot driver, Hardware Limitations) – an analog read competes with the Wi-Fi driver

33.name: IO0
33.hint: strapping pin GPIO0: high at reset = SPI boot, low (with GPIO2 low) = download boot; weak pull-up at reset (datasheet table 4, 6); ADC2: shared with Wi-Fi (ESP-IDF v6.1 ADC oneshot driver, Hardware Limitations) – an analog read competes with the Wi-Fi driver

34.name: IO2
34.hint: strapping pin GPIO2: any level for SPI boot, must be low for download boot; weak pull-down at reset (datasheet table 4, 6); ADC2: shared with Wi-Fi (ESP-IDF v6.1 ADC oneshot driver, Hardware Limitations) – an analog read competes with the Wi-Fi driver

35.name: IO15
35.hint: strapping pin MTDO: low at reset disables the U0TXD boot messages, with GPIO5 it sets the SDIO slave timing; weak pull-up at reset (datasheet table 4, 7, 8); ADC2: shared with Wi-Fi (ESP-IDF v6.1 ADC oneshot driver, Hardware Limitations) – an analog read competes with the Wi-Fi driver

36.name: D1
36.hint: GPIO8: the flash pins, not led out of the ESP32-WROVER-E (ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 table 3, pins 17–22, note 2) – the header pin carries nothing here

37.name: D0
37.hint: GPIO7: the flash pins, not led out of the ESP32-WROVER-E (ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 table 3, pins 17–22, note 2) – the header pin carries nothing here

38.name: CLK
38.hint: GPIO6: the flash pins, not led out of the ESP32-WROVER-E (ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 table 3, pins 17–22, note 2) – the header pin carries nothing here

hints: WROVER-E: the supply of the module must deliver at least 0.5 A (datasheet table 14, IVDD); Wi-Fi TX peaks at 350 mA (table 16, 802.11b at 19.5 dBm)
GPIO16 and GPIO17 belong to the WROVER-E's PSRAM and GPIO6–GPIO11 to its flash: the header pins IO16, IO17, D0–D3, CMD and CLK carry nothing usable
power the board through one and only one of micro-USB, 5V and 3V3 (DevKitC V4, 1.1.4): a 5 V supply at the 5V pin and a USB cable at the same time feed each other unless a diode blocks the way

radio.source: ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4: table 19 (Wi-Fi centre frequencies 2412–2484 MHz), table 20 (802.11b TX power 19.5 dBm typ), table 25 (Bluetooth LE 2402–2480 MHz, −12 … +9 dBm)

sources: pin numbers and names, footprint, mpn, jlc_class: EasyEDA library data of C20437001 (edakit part import, 2026-11-03) – J2 pins 1–19 as 1–19, J3 pins 1–19 as 20–38

ESP32 esp-dev-kits Documentation, Release master (Espressif, 2025-11-24), 1.1 ESP32-DevKitC V4 – LCSC product data of C20437001, https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/dc33f4253b78a0ac5625f7849073d2d3.pdf?productCode=C20437001, read 2026-11-03: the versions of the board (ESP32-WROVER-E among the modules), 1.1.4 power supply options (micro-USB, 5V and GND, 3V3 and GND – mutually exclusive), 1.1.5 header block J2 and J3 (names and functions), note 3 (GPIO16 and GPIO17 reserved on the boards with ESP32-WROVER modules)

ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 (Espressif, https://documentation.espressif.com/esp32-wrover-e_esp32-wrover-ie_datasheet_en.pdf, read 2026-11-03): table 3 pin definitions (pins 17–22 and 27–28 NC), 4.2 MTDI selects VDD_SDIO, table 13 VDD33 abs. max 3.6 V, table 14 VDD33 3.0–3.6 V, IVDD ≥ 0.5 A, −40 … 85 °C, table 15 DC characteristics (VIH ≥ 0.75 × VDD up to VDD + 0.3 V, VIL ≤ 0.25 × VDD, VOH ≥ 0.8 × VDD, IOL 28 mA typ, RPU/RPD 45 kΩ, VIL_nRST ≤ 0.6 V), table 16 (TX 802.11b 350 mA peak), tables 19, 20, 25 (radio)

the board's own circuit – AMS1117-3.3 from EXT_5V (the 5V pin) to VDD33 (the 3V3 pin), the BAT760 from VBUS to EXT_5V, EN with 10 kΩ / 100 nF and the EN button's 100 nF: ESP32-DevKitC V4 schematic Rev V4 (2017-12-06), https://dl.espressif.com/dl/schematics/esp32_devkitc_v4-sch.pdf, as transcribed in tests/open_designs/esp32-devkitc-v4
dropout_v 1.3: the AMS1117-3.3's maximum dropout at 0.8 A (its datasheet p. 3, as the library entry C6186) – the board's regulator
vin_min_v 4.3: the module's least VDD33 of 3.0 V (WROVER-E table 14) plus the AMS1117's 1.3 V dropout – assumption: the DevKitC documentation names the 5V pin's supply '5 V' and gives no range
i_core_a 0.35: the WROVER-E's 802.11b TX peak (table 16) as the upper bound – the board's power LED (about 1.5 mA through 2 kΩ) and the CP2102N (powered from 3V3) are not added

the GPIO pins (types, functions, strapping pins, pulls, ADC ranges, hints) are the ESP32's as the library entry C701341 (ESP32-WROOM-32E, the same ESP32 chip) gives them, renamed to the header's names (VP, VN, TX, RX); the WROVER-E's pin table (ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4 table 3) lists the same functions for these GPIOs

decoupling default switched off for this entry (needs.decoupling false): the board carries its own capacitors – 22 µF on EXT_5V (the 5V pin) and 22 µF on VDD33 (the 3V3 pin), C1 and C3 of the DevKitC V4 schematic, as transcribed in tests/open_designs/esp32-devkitc-v4
gpio_i_max_a 0.028, gpio_i_total_max_a 1.2, pin and gpio_v_max_v 3.6: as C701341 (IOL typ at maximum drive, the ESP32 Series Datasheet's cumulative IO current, VDD + 0.3 V)
notes: Espressif's development board with the ESP32-WROVER-E (8 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM), plugged into the ADLSC carrier with 2 × 19 sockets. Its own regulator, USB bridge and buttons are on the board: the carrier sees the header pins only.

verified.datasheet: ESP32 esp-dev-kits Documentation, Release master (Espressif, 2025-11-24), 1.1 ESP32-DevKitC V4; ESP32-WROVER-E & ESP32-WROVER-IE Datasheet v2.4
checked: header J2/J3 names and order (1.1.5) against the EasyEDA symbol of C20437001: J2 = 1–19, J3 = 20–38
power options 1.1.4: micro-USB, 5V/GND, 3V3/GND, one and only one
WROVER-E table 3: GPIO6–11 not led out (pins 17–22 NC), pins 27/28 NC (PSRAM)
WROVER-E tables 13–16: VDD33 3.0–3.6 V, IVDD ≥ 0.5 A, VIH 0.75 × VDD, VIL 0.25 × VDD, TX peak 350 mA
radio: 2412–2484 MHz, 19.5 dBm typ (802.11b); Bluetooth LE 2402–2480 MHz

antenna_dbi of the WROVER-E's PCB antenna: not in the datasheet (2.33 dBi is the WROVER-IE's external antenna) – LIM.eirp cannot be computed

the DevKitC's operating temperature: not given (the WROVER-E alone: −40 … 85 °C)
REACH and RoHS of the board: not read
